claims.text: In-situ oxidation testing can be used to improve oxidation resistance in high-entropy alloys.
In-situ oxidation testing allows real-time study of oxidation behavior.
Real-time study of oxidation behavior enables optimization of alloy composition and processing conditions.
Oxide-layer formation and element diffusion are structural mediators of oxidation behavior in the proposed HEAs.
The proposed method is intended for high-temperature conditions.
Optimization of alloy composition and processing conditions will produce improved oxidation resistance in HEAs.
The extent to which in-situ oxidation testing can improve HEA oxidation resistance is uncertain and requires further research.

contradictions.description: The intervention is only a testing/monitoring method, but the predicted outcome is direct improvement of a material property. No actual composition or processing optimization is specified or applied, and the experiment compares testing methods rather than optimized versus non-optimized alloys.
